title: Viharini Sarvopari Shiritaaj - Shri Ali Madhuri Ji, Shri Nikunj Keli Madhuri
sanskrit_text: Viharini Sarvopari Shiritaja. [1] Rahat Bihari Ajnyakari, Sahachari Sang Samaj. Kunj Nikunjana Rasamaya Punjana, Sahaja Bhari Sukhasaja. [2]Vana Rajadhani Rasa Sarasani, Adbhuta Achala Suraja.Alimadhuri Kripa Drishti Se, Pure Tana Mana Kaja. [3]- Shri Ali Madhuri Ji, Shri Nikunj Keli MadhuriO Śrī Vihāriṇī Jī (Śrī Rādhā)! You alone are the highest of all and the crowned sovereign above everyone. [1]Even Śrī Bihārī Jī (Śrī Kṛṣṇa) Himself always follows Your command, while your sakhīs (companions) remain with you as your loving circle. In every grove and secret bower (kuñj–nikuñj), there is an abundance of rasa. Everything is effortlessly adorned with bliss. [2]Śrī Vṛndāvana Dhāma is Your royal capital, overflowing with sweetness, where Your sovereignty reigns without interruption. Śrī Alī Mādhurī Jī declares that by just a single glance of Śrī Rādhā Mahārāṇī Jū, all the pursuits of body and mind are instantly fulfilled. [3]

title: Yahi Rasmay Nam Sau Rakhat Prem Apar - Shri Hit Kishori Lal, Radha Sudha Nidhi Stva (94.2)
sanskrit_text: Yahi Ras-may Nam Sau, Rakhat Prem Apar. Lagat Tuchchh Purusharth Sab, Yeh Aagein Sukumar.- Shri Hit Kishori Lal, Radha Sudha Nidhi Stva (94.2)Before the supremely nectarean Name “Rādhā,” even the four exalted pursuits of life — dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa — lose their significance. This sacred and rasa-filled Name of Rādhā is the one Śrī Kṛṣṇa loves most deeply in His heart.

This sacred and rasa-filled Name of Rādhā is the one Śrī Kṛṣṇa loves most deeply in His heart.
author: Braj Rasik Heritage

sanskrit_text: (Rag-Kafi) Suniyen Araj Hamari, Shri Vrishbhanu Kumari. Darasan Dehu Daya Kariken Mohi, Pritam-Pran-Adhar. [1] Kunj Mahal Niju Sajani Ke Sang, Tahal Karau Sukumari. Radhaballabh ‘Hit Paramanand’, Ai Mili Rijhavari. [2]- Shri Hita Parmanand Das, Sri Hita Parmanand Das Ji Ki Vani, Padavali (87)O Śrī Vṛṣabhānu-nandinī, Śrī Rādhā, please accept my humble plea. title: Vyas Rasik Nirnay Kiyo - Shri Lalit Kishori Dev Ju Ki Vani, Siddhant Ki Saakhi (356)
sanskrit_text: Vyas Rasik Nirnay Kiyo, Shrvrindavan Maanhi.Shri Swami Ke Dharm Kon, Patatar Kon Koi Nahin.- Shri Lalit Kishori Dev, Shri Lalit Kishori Dev Ju Ki Vani, Siddhant Ki Saakhi (356)Śrī Harirāma Vyāsa Jī, through deep contemplation among the assembly of rasikas in Śrī Vṛndāvana Dhāma, concluded that there is no path equal to the uninterrupted nitya-vihāra upāsanā of the divine couple, revealed by the incomparable master, Śrī Svāmī Haridāsa Jī. This path, in which the couple is exclusively and unceasingly worshipped in the state of their intimate love-plays, is utterly unparalleled.

title: Arati Kije Sundarvar Ki - Shri Biharin Dev Ju Ki Vani, Ras Ke Pada (39)
sanskrit_text: Arati Kijai Sundarvar Ki.Nagar Naval Nikunj Indu Jug, Akhil Taap Tam Har Ki. [1]Nav Vilas Mridu Haas Manohar, Shravat Sudha Sukh Kar Ki.‘Shri Biharidas’ Lochan Chakor Nit, Ans Priya Bhuj Dhar Ki. [2]- Shri Biharin Dev Ji, Shri Biharin Dev Ju Ki Vani, Ras Ke Pada (39)Perform the ārati of the beautiful, ever-youthful divine couple. This ever-fresh rasika couple shines like twin moons within the Nikunja, dispelling all sorrow and the darkness of ignorance from the hearts of devotees. [1]From their ever-new love-plays and gentle, enchanting smiles flows a stream of nectar that bestows bliss. Svāmī Śrī Bihārinadāsa Jī says that the chakora-birds of my eyes ceaselessly drink the nectar of the vision where Śyāmasundara has placed His arm upon the shoulders of His beloved Śrī Rādhā. [2]

title: Agra Kaam Harinam Se Sankat Hota Sahay - Shri Agradas, Agragranthawali
sanskrit_text: ‘Agra’ Kaam Harinam Se, Sankat Hota Sahay.Kou Kahu Ko Nahin, Dekho Thok Bajay.- Shri Agradas, Agragranthawali Śrī Agrādāsa Jī declares that only the Holy Name of Śrī Hari is the true well-wisher of the soul, which alone serves as a true companion in times of every distress. No one truly belongs to another in this world; you may test this reality thoroughly and see for yourself.

title: Chale Piy Bhaavati Ras Len - Goswami Shri Harirai Ji
sanskrit_text: (Raag Vihag)Chale Piy Bhaavati Ras Len.Khel Phag Anuraag Badhyo Hai, Mahamatt Gati Men. [1]Jheen Basan Gulaal Son Sagamge, Tan Raajat Dyuti Ain.Rasik Preetam Piy Pyaari Podhe, Nav Nikunj Sukh Sen. [2]- Goswami Shri Hariray JiLord Śrī Kṛṣṇa joins His soul-beloved Śrī Rādhā to relish the nectar of divine love. Through the play of phāga (Holī), their mutual affection has intensified so greatly that their gait has become as intoxicated and graceful as that of Cupid himself. [1]Their fine, delicate garments are thoroughly drenched in the hues of gulāl, causing the splendor of their divine forms to shine with unparalleled brilliance. Finally, the Rasika Beloved and His dear Kiśorī Jī rest together upon the blissful bed within the fresh forest groves of Nikunja, says Gosvāmī Śrī Harirāya Jī. [2].

title: Sab Ras Kau Ras Prem Hai Vishayi Khele Saar - Sri Surdas, Soor Sagar
sanskrit_text: Sajan Kutumb Parijan Badhe, Sut Dara Dhan Dham.Mahamudha Vishayi Bhayo, Chit Akarsho Kaam.- Sri Surdas, Soor Sagar (325.21)O deluded soul! As your family expanded — as dear ones, children, spouse, wealth, and prosperity increased — so too did you sink ever deeper into the enjoyment of worldly pleasures, to the point that you forgot the true purpose of your life. O foolish one! Do you truly believe temporary wealth is the measure of real success? Remember — your birth was meant solely for the upliftment of your own soul.

title: Vrindavan Mahima Aparampar - Shri Radhacharan Das, Vrindavan Virudavali (32)
sanskrit_text: Vrindavan Mahima Aparampar.Shyamsundar Bhokta Ras Shyama Vrindavan Aadhar. [1]Teenon Teenon Ka Poorak Mili Hobat Nitya Vihar.Do Mile Ek Nahin Sang Hove To Nahin Leela Vistar. [2]Do Mile Kurukshetra Mein Phir Bhi Nahin Hiy Ras Sanchar.Vrindavan Tan Praan Hain Radha Man Hain Nandkumar. [3]Bhajahu Sang Kari In Teennan Tab Hovai Sukh Sakar.‘Radhacharan Das’ Binu Inke Ras Sadhan Bekar. [4]- Shri Radhacharan Das, Vrindavan Virudavali (32)The glory of Śrī Vṛndāvana Dhāma is immeasurable. Here, Śyāmasundara is the enjoyer who relishes divine rasa, Śrī Śyāmā Jī (Rādhā) is the very embodiment of that rasa, and Vṛndāvana is the very foundation of their love-plays. [1]These three — Rādhā, Kṛṣṇa, and Vṛndāvana — are mutually complementary, and only through their harmonious union is the eternal nitya-vihāra rasa manifest. If even one of these three is not present with the others, the eternal play of divine love cannot unfold. [2]Although Śrī Rādhā and Śrī Kṛṣṇa once met at Kurukṣetra, the intimate nectar of Nikunja-rasa did not arise there, for the sacred realm of Vṛndāvana was absent. Vṛndāvana is the body, Rādhā is the life-breath, and Śrī Kṛṣṇa is the mind within that divine whole. [3]Śrī Rādhācaraṇadāsa declares that only when a soul worships all three together — Rādhā, Kṛṣṇa, and Vṛndāvana — does one truly relish the nectar of the eternal nitya-vihāra; without this unified devotion, such rasa-upāsanā remains incomplete. [4]

title: Shrivrrindavipineshvari Hrridigatam Premaiva - Shri Govardhan Bhatt, Shri Radhakund Stava (47)
sanskrit_text: Shrivrrindavipineshvari Hrridigatam Premaiva Kundachchalat Manye Prasvadantare.aparimitam Vrriddham Bhrrisham Nirgatam. Yad‌gopala Varenyasunusahitan Sarvan SvashobhachayaiMurchcha Prapayati Pramodasudhaya Krritva Kila Kshalitan.- Shri Govardhan Bhatt, Shri Radhakund Stava (47)It is my firm faith that the divine love of Śrī Rādhā's heart, the Queen of Vṛndāvana, has manifested as the sacred Śrī Rādhākuṇḍa. That boundless love swells and overflows without limit. By the flood of its beauty, it causes even Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the exalted son of Nanda, along with all, to faint in divine ecstasy, and then bathes them in transcendental bliss, completely purifying and refreshing them.

title: Dou Magan Bhaye Ras Hori Mein - Shri Roop Madhuri Ji Ki Vani, Padavali (172)
sanskrit_text: (Rag Dhamal Va Hori Ka Rasiya)Dou Magan Bhaye Ras Hori Mein.Dai Galbaiyan Lal Ladaiti, Bandhe Prem Ki Dori Mein. [1]Mridu Muskavat Chit Churavat, Len Gulal Kar Jhori Mein.“Roop Madhuri” Rang Badho Hai, Kunwar Kishor Kishori Mein. [2]- Shri Roop Madhuri, Shri Roop Madhuri Ji Ki Vani, Padavali (172)Both the Beloveds have become utterly absorbed in the nectar of Holī. Placing their arms around each other’s necks, the youthful Lord and His Darling Rādhā appear bound together by the unbreakable thread of divine love. [1]With gentle smiles, they steal each other's hearts while taking handfuls of gulāl from their bags. Srī Rūpamādhurī says that the intensity of this love continues to deepen between the youthful Kiśora and Kiśorī. [2]

title: Jivan Muktan Ko Jahan Hai Nahin Adhikar - Shri Charandas

title: Hori Mein Laj Na Rahe Pyari - Shri Lalit Ladaiti, Shri Kishori Kripa Kataksha, Varshotsav Pad (35)
sanskrit_text: (Rag Sarang Rasiya)Hori Mein Laj Na Rahe Pyari.Rasiya Phirat Bajavat Dafli, Gavat Laj Bhari Gari. [1]Muth Gulal Itai Ut Phenkat, Gail Rok Rahyo Braj Nari.Lalit Ladaiti Kathin Hai Bachivo, Chhail Karat Udham Bhari. [2]- Shri Lalit Ladaiti, Shri Kishori Kripa Kataksha, Varshotsav Pad (35)O Sakhī! In this festival of Holi, there is no place left for shyness or restraint. The divine Rasiya (Śrī Kṛṣṇa) wanders about playing His tambourine (ḍaphalī), singing songs filled with playful and teasing jests. [1]Throwing handfuls of crimson gulāl here and there, He has blocked the path of the women of Vraja. Śrī Lalita Laḍaitī says, It is difficult to escape now, for that mischievous boy is causing a great, joyful chaos today. [2]

title: Jakon Kahiye Mudh Jag - Shri Nagridas Ji (Maharaj Sawant Singh) Ji Ki Vani
sanskrit_text: Jakon Kahiye Moodh Jag, Dukh Daun Laagi Her.Jamuna Vrindavipin Taji, Dhavat Beekaner.- Shri Nagridas Ji (Maharaj Sawant Singh)Those who abandon the sacred banks of Śrī Yamunā and the rasa-filled abode of Vṛndāvana, and instead rush toward places like Bīkāner or elsewhere in pursuit of worldly pleasures, are the true fools — as if forsaking infinite bliss, they rush towards the very flames of suffering.

title: Kunj Mahal Rang Ho Ho Hori- Shri Vanshi Ali Ji, Varshotsav, Basant Ke Pad (15)
sanskrit_text: (Rag Gauri)Kunj Mahal Rang Ho Ho Hori,Khelat Naval Kishor Kishori.Bajat Taal Mridang Jhajh Dhap,Abir Gulal Udaavat Jhori. [1]Naachat Sakhi Jan Jhamak Mil Mil,Gavati Gari Lal Saun Jori.Hansat Hansavati Nij Swamin Ko,Shri Lalit Sakhi Jaishri ‘Banshi Ali’ Mori. [2]- Shri Vanshi Ali Ji, Varshotsav, Basant Ke Pad (15)In the kuṃja mahala (palace of the groves), the festival of Holī is in full bloom, where the eternally youthful pair, Śrī Rādhā Kṛṣṇa, are joyfully playing the Holī of divine love. The rhythms of tāla, mṛdaṅga (a double-sided drum), jhāñjha (cymbals), and ḍapha (tambourine) are being played, while heaps of abīra (scented powder) and gulāl (red powder) are being thrown by the sakhī’s. [1]The sakhīs dance together with rhythmic harmony, collectively singing playful and teasing songs (gārī) directed at the Beloved Śrī Lāla Jī. Śrī Vanśī Ali’s guru, Śrī Lalitā Sakhī, is laughing heartily and also bringing smiles to Her Sovereign Queen Śrī Rādhā during this celebration. [2]

title: Vyas Na Vyapak Dekhiye Nirgun Pare Na Jaani - Shri Hariram Vyas, Vyas Vani, Siddhant Ki Saakhi (07)
sanskrit_text: Vyas Na Vyapak Dekhiye, Nirgun Pare Na Jaani.Tab Bhaktani Hita Autare, (Shri) Radhavallabh Aani.- Shri Hariram Vyas, Vyas Vani, Saakhi (07)Śrī Harirāma Vyāsa Jī declares that the Supreme Brahma, being all-pervading, remains invisible to the mundane eyes, and being beyond attributes (nirguṇa), is incomprehensible to the intellect. Thus, for the welfare of His devotees and to grant them the relish of divine rasa, that Supreme Personality has manifested visibly in the form of Śrī Rādhāvallabha.

title: Aaj Khelen Hori Nav Nagari -  Shri Govindsharan Devacharya Ji Ki Vani (151)
sanskrit_text: (Rag Paraj)Aaj Khelen Hori Nav Nagari.Saras Gulal Dar Pritam Pai, Sakal Kala Gun Agari. [1]Shri Vrishbhan Bhavan Mein Sajni, Phaili Rahyo Anurag Ri.Kirti Kul Kirti Gavati Lakhi, Gobind Saran Badhbhag Ri. [2]- Shri Govind Sharan Devacharya, Shri Govindsharan Devacharya Ji Ki Vani (151)Today, the ever-youthful, Śrī Rādhā Nāgarī, is playing Holī. She, who is the foremost adept in all arts and virtues, showers delightful gulāla (red powder) upon Her beloved Śyāmasundara. [1]O sakhī! Within the palace of Śrī Vṛṣabhānu, a divine love is overflowing everywhere. The entire lineage of Mother Kīrti (the family and companions) is singing the glories of Śrī Rādhā; beholding this sight, Śrī Govindaśaraṇa considers himself most fortunate. [2]

title: Kaam Na Aave Kaun Hu - Shri Biharin Dev Ji Ki Vani, Siddhant Ki Saakhi (364)
sanskrit_text: Kaam Na Aavai Kaun Hoon, Ati Aparas Aachaar.Ant Nibaahai Prem Heen, Chhaande Khaat Kau Dwar.- Shri Biharin Dev Ji, Shri Biharin Dev Ji Ki Vani, Siddhant Ki Saakhi (364)Many people remain entangled throughout their lives in notions of saparasa and aparasa, or in external practices and rituals. At the moment of death, nothing proves of any use. Only the pure love offered to the Lord sustains; nothing else. That love alone has the power to carry the soul across the vast ocean of illusion.

title: Lagyo Neh Sab Bhanti Nibhaiho - Shri Bhori Sakhi, Prem Ki Peer (415)
sanskrit_text: Lagyo Neh Sab Bhanti Nibhaiho.Ye Mere Man Sudridh Bharoso, Baanh Gahe Ki Laaj Lajaeho. [1]Lok Ved Parlok Jati Kul, Paap Punya Dukh Dvand Chhudeho.‘Bhori’ Apni Jani Kripa Kari, Shri Pad Pankaj Subas Basaiho. [2]- Shri Bhori Sakhi, Prem Ki Peer (415)O dearest Pyārī Jū (Śrī Rādhā), now that the sacred knot of love has been tied between us, I trust completely that You will sustain it. I know that by Your merciful nature, anyone whose hand You accept becomes Yours forever. Surely You will preserve the honor of one who has surrendered at Your feet. [1]Śrī Bhorī Sakhī humbly prays: bestow such grace that, freeing me from the constraints of worldly decorum, the bindings of the Vedas, fear of the next world, pride of family and status, and the dualities of sin and virtue, I may dwell eternally at the refuge of Your lotus feet. [2]

title: Daya Prem Unmat Je Tann Ki Tani Sudhi Nahin - Shri Dayabai
sanskrit_text: ‘Daya’ Prem Unmatt Je, Tan Ki Tani Sudhi Naahin.Jhuke Rahein Hari Ras Chhake, Thake Nem Vrat Naahin.- Shri DayabaiDayābāī says that those who are absorbed in divine love of God lose all awareness of bodily consciousness. They are so immersed in the nectar of Śrī Hari that external injunctions and prohibitions, vows, and ritual observances no longer hold any special significance for them.

title: Aaj Sakhi Van Ki Sobha Dekhi - Sri Thakur Das Ju Ki Vani, Pad (3)
sanskrit_text: Aaj Sakhi Van Ki Sobha Dekhi.Vimal Kamal Rang Ati Phule, Jamuna Jalhi Visekhi. [1]Saras Hans Paraspar Naachat, Kok Paphahiya Pekhi.Mor Chakor Sor Pik Bhavai, Gaavat Ati Ras Rekhi. [2]Lata Lalit Chahun Disi Ras Jhoomin, Inki Taraf Nirekhi.Thakur Sakhi Ya Chhabi Ko Dekhat, Shri Haridas Samekhi. [3]- Shri Thakur Das, Sri Thakur Das Ju Ki Vani, Pad (3)A sakhī tells her friend: “O friend! Witness the unmatched beauty of Vṛndāvana’s forest today! In the sacred waters of Śrī Yamunā, the lotuses bloom fully, a truly enchanting sight.” [1]Cranes and swans dance gracefully, while the cuckoo and papihā delight all hearts. The harmonious calls of peacocks, partridges, and cuckoos fill the air with songs of love. [2]Beautiful creepers sway joyfully in all directions. Śrī Ṭhākura Sakhī says that the sakhīs behold this transcendental vision, where Svāmī Śrī Haridāsa is present alongside His worshipful deities, Śrī Kunjabihārī and Śrī Kunja Biharīṇī. [3]

title: Khelat Faag Lakhyo Piy Pyari Ko - Shri Raskhan, Raskhan Ratnavali
sanskrit_text: (Savaiya)Khelat Faag Lakhyo Piy Pyari Ko, Ta Mukh Ki Upma Kihin Dijiye.Dekhat Hi Bani Aavai Bhalai, Rasikhan Kaha Hai Jo Baar Na Kijiye. [1]Jyaun Jyaun Chhabili Kahai Pichkari Lai, Ek Lai Yah Doosri Leejai.Tyaun Tyaun Chhabilo Chhke Chhabi Chaak So, Here Hanse Na Tare Kharo Bhije. [2]- Shri Raskhan, Raskhan RatnawaliA sakhī, describing the Phāg Līlā to her sakhi, says: “O friend! I have witnessed Kṛṣṇa and His beloved Rādhā playing Holī. How can one even attempt to compare the beauty of their faces? That vision alone is enough to captivate the heart; what object in the world could not be offered in reverence before such a sight?” [1]As the playful Śrī Rādhā wields Her water-gun, saying, “Take this one, and now take this other,” the charming Śyāmasundara becomes ever more intoxicated with the nectar of Her unparalleled beauty. sanskrit_text: Kab In Nayananitai Lakhun, Vrindavan Ki Dhoori.Jo Rasikaniki Param Priya, Paavan Jeevan Moori.- Shri Prabhudutt Brahmachari, Sri Vrindavan Mahatmya (2)When shall I, with these very eyes, behold that supremely sacred ‘raja’ (sand) of Vṛndāvana — the raja that is supremely dear to the rasikas and the very source of their lives?

title: Sakhi Sab Hve Gaye Laalhi Laal - Jagadguru Shri Kripalu Ji Maharaj, Prem Ras Madira, Hori Madhuri (24)
sanskrit_text: Sakhi! Sab, Hvai Gaye Laalhin Laal.Aiso Rang Chalyo Pichkarin, Aiso Udayo Gulaal. [1]Laali Laal, Laal Bhaye Laalhun, Laal Bhain Brajbaal.Taruwar Laal, Laal Bhaye Sarwar, Shuk, Pik Laal Maraal. [2]Dhenu Laal Brajrenu Laal Bhai, Laal Bhaye Sab Gwaal.Baahar Laal ‘Kripalu’ Faag Ko, Bheetar Laal Gupaal. [3]- Jagadguru Shri Kripalu Ji Maharaj, Prem Ras Madira, Hori Madhuri (24)A sakhī, describing the Holī festival of Vṛndāvana to her intimate companion, says: “O friend! In the Holī of the divine couple, such streams of colored water were sprayed from waterguns, and such clouds of crimson powder arose, that everything was dyed red.” [1]Śyāmasundara became red, Kiśorī Jī too became red, the maidens of Braja were colored alike, and even the trees and lakes were covered in red. Parrots, cuckoos, and swans — all were transformed into the same hue. [2]All the cows and even the sacred dust of Braja were reddened, and every cowherd boy was covered in that same color. Jagadguru Śrī Kṛpālu Jī Mahārāja explains that outwardly all were colored by the red of Holī, yet inwardly every heart was drenched in loving devotion of Lāḍilī–Lāla. [3]

title: Ved Bhed Paayo Nahin - Shri Bhartendu Harishchandra, Bhartendu Granthawali, Bhakta Sarvasva (8)
sanskrit_text: Ved Bhed Paayo Nahin, Bhae Puran Puran.Smritihu Ki Sab Smriti Gai, Pai Na Mile Bhagwan.- Shri Bhartendu Harishchandra, Bhartendu Granthawali, Bhakta Sarvasva (8)The Vedas failed to grasp His mystery, and the Purāṇas grew ancient in their search, yet could not fathom His depth. The Smṛtis lost all consciousness attempting to comprehend Him. The essence is that the realization of God is possible only through selfless love and complete surrender (śaraṇāgati).

title: Brindaban Khelat Hari Hori - Sri Surdas, Soor Sagar
sanskrit_text: (Raag Kalyan)Brindaban Khelat Hari Hori.Bajat Taal Mridang Jhanjh Daf, Nand Lala Vrishbhanu Kishori. [1]Haun Apnai Grih Tain Nikasi Sakhi, Saas Ki Traas Nanad Ki Chori.Aur Sakhi Sab Chhandi Syaam Mo, Kar Marori Pahunchi Gahi Tori. [2]Syaam Baran Ati Sundar Sanwaro, Kanak Badan Radhe Tanu Gori.Surdas Ke Prabhu Doou Raajat, Paaras Kanchan Ki Si Jori. [3]- Sri Surdas, Soor SagarIn Vṛndāvana, Lord Hari (Śrī Kṛṣṇa)  is joyfully playing Holī. The rhythms of tāla, mṛdaṅga (a double-sided drum), jhāñjha (cymbals), and ḍapha (tambourine) are being played in every direction, as Nandalāla (Kṛṣṇa) and Vṛṣabhānu-kiśorī (Rādhā) together celebrate the festival in delight. [1]O sakhī! With great difficulty, I escaped my house, avoiding the watchful eyes of my mother-in-law and sister-in-law. There, Śyāmsundara left aside all the other sakhīs and grabbed only my hand, gently twisting it in loving mischief. [2]Sūradāsa says: the dark handsome Kṛṣṇa and molten gold like Rādhā, shine together like the touchstone and gold paired as one. [3]

title: Vamukh Ki Aasha Lagi - Shri Madhuri Das, Utkantha Madhuri (28)
sanskrit_text: Vamukh Ki Aasha Lagi, Taji Aas Sab Jog.Ab Swasa Hu Tajegi, Jo Na Bane Sanjog.- Shri Madhuri Das, Utkantha Madhuri (28)My longing is solely for the darśana of the lotus-like faces of the divine couple, Śrī Rādhā–Kṛṣṇa. title: Namo Namo Ju Bhakti Rijhvaar - Shri Vrindavan Das Ji
sanskrit_text: Namo Namo Ju Bhakti Rijhvaar.Naam Vidit Gopeshwar Jinkau,Te Vrinda Kanan Kutuvaar. [1]Yaatra Sufal Hot Bas Jabahin,Jo Raj Vandai In Darbaar.‘Vrindavan Hit’ Roop Sakhi Vapu,Sevat Dampati Nitya Vihaar. [2]- Shri Hita Vrindavan DasI bow again and again to that Lord Śiva who is pleased solely by ‘Bhakti’ (devotion). Renowned throughout the world as Gopeśvara — the Lord of the gopīs — He stands as the guardian and protector of Vṛndāvana. [1]A pilgrimage to Braj is considered truly successful only when one comes before Gopeśvara, beholds His darśana, and places upon one’s head the sacred dust of this holy place. Śrī Hita Vṛndāvana Dāsa declares that Gopeśvara Mahādeva assumes the form of a sakhī within the forest bowers, where he serves the divine couple, Śrī Rādhā Kṛṣṇa, and drinks the nectar of Their eternal Nitya Vihāra Rasa. [2]

title: Hai Hari Te Harinam Badero - Shri Gadadhar Bhatt Ji Ki Vani (15)
sanskrit_text: Hai Hari Ten Harinam Badero, Tako Moodh Karat Kat Jhero.Pragat Daras Muchukundahi Deenho, Tahu Ayusu Bho Tap Kero.Sut-Hit Naam Ajamila Leeno, Ya Bhav Mein Na Kiyo Phiri Phero. [1]Par-Apavad Svad Jiyo Rachyo, Vritha Karat Bakvad Ghanero.Tako Dasyo Ans ‘Gadadhar’, Hari Hari Kahat Jat Kaha Tero. [2]- Shri Gadadhar Bhatt Ji, Shri Gadadhar Bhatt Ji Ki Vani (15)The Holy Name of Lord Hari is even greater than Hari Himself. O foolish one, why do you hesitate to accept this truth? Consider the evidence—King Mucakuṇda was granted direct darśana of the Lord, yet he was instructed to continue his austerities. However, the sinful Ajāmila merely called out the name “Nārāyaṇa” while addressing his son, and by the power of that very Name, the attendants of Viṣṇu came to protect him. Thereafter, engaging in devotion, he became forever freed from the cycle of birth and death. Thus, the merciful Name of the Lord was the guiding mentor in his redemption. [1]Why do you waste your time in meaningless talk and worldly gossip? Śrī Gadādhara Jī says: Of the time you waste in meaningless talks, if even one-tenth were spent chanting “Hari, Hari,” what harm would come to you? Even a slight effort in this direction would secure your highest good. [2]

title: Naam Liyain Patik Katein - Shri Guruchauna Ji Maharaj
sanskrit_text: Naam Liyain Patik Katen, Pahunchai Hari Ke Des.‘Chhauna’ Ke Girahi Japau, Kai Ateet Ke Bhes.- Shri Guruchauna Ji MaharajThrough chanting the Holy Name of the Lord, all sins are destroyed, and the soul ultimately reaches the sacred abode of Hari. Śrī Chaunā Jī Mahārāja teaches that whether one is a householder or a renunciate, the fruit of the Name is the same. External form or attire has no real importance; the essence lies entirely in sincere remembrance of the Divine Name.

title: Priya Piy Chhabi Lakhi Chhakani Chhakayi - Shri Sarasmadhuri
sanskrit_text: (Raag Vihag)Priya Piy Chhabi Lakhi Chhakani Chhakayi.Phaag Khel Khilavaar Paraspar, Tanaman Mudit Mahayi. [1]Yugmachand Sahchari Chakori, Prem Preeti Pragatayi.Sarasmadhuri Saanvri Gori, Jori Drigan Basayi. [2]- Shri SarasmadhuriŚrī Priyā (Rādhā) and Her beloved Priyatama (Kṛṣṇa) gaze upon one another’s beauty and are utterly intoxicated in love. Absorbed in the playful sport of Holī, Their bodies and hearts are immersed in the nectar of this divine festival. [1]Just as the chakora bird fixes its longing gaze upon the moon, so the sakhīs, like devoted chakorīs, behold this divine Yugala-chandra (Śrī Rādhā Kṛṣṇa) lovingly. Śrī Sarasamādhurī declares that this unparalleled pair of dark and fair complexion has permanently enshrined within his eyes. [2]

[2]- Shri SarasmadhuriŚrī Priyā (Rādhā) and Her beloved Priyatama (Kṛṣṇa) gaze upon one another’s beauty and are utterly intoxicated in love. Absorbed in the playful sport of Holī, Their bodies and hearts are immersed in the nectar of this divine festival. [1]Just as the chakora bird fixes its longing gaze upon the moon, so the sakhīs, like devoted chakorīs, behold this divine Yugala-chandra (Śrī Rādhā Kṛṣṇa) lovingly. Śrī Sarasamādhurī declares that this unparalleled pair of dark and fair complexion has permanently enshrined within his eyes. [2]
author: Braj Rasik Heritage

title: Priya Badan Sukhma Sadan - Shri Harivyas Devacharya, Mahavani, Sewa Sukh (05)
sanskrit_text: Priya Badan Sukhma Sadan, Rahyo Prem Paripoori.Ja Madhi Preetam Praan Ki, Sarbas Jeevani Moori.- Shri Harivyas Devacharya, Mahavani, Sewa Sukh (05)The lotus-face of Śrī Rādhā is the abode of bliss, filled with divine love, where the life-breath of Her beloved, Śrī Kṛṣṇa resides. Indeed, it alone is the source of life of His very existence.

title: Rangili Galin Bich Ho Ho Hori - Shri Nagridas Ji Ki Vani, Utsav Mala (143)
sanskrit_text: Rangili Galin Bich Ho Ho Hori.It Nandanandan Rasik Ladilo, Ut Vrishbhan Kisori. [1]Udat Gulal Kachhu Nahin Soojhat, Jhakjhoro Jhakjhori.Nagaridas Paraspar Dharat, Bhar Bhar Kanak Kamori. [2]- Shri Nagridas Ji (Maharaj Sawant Singh Ji), Shri Nagridas Ji Ki Vani, Utsav Mala (143)In the Raṇgīlī galī of Barsānā, the festival of Holī is being celebrated with boundless joy. On one side stands the charming son of Nanda, the rasika Śrī Kṛṣṇa; on the other side is Vṛṣabhānu’s beloved daughter, Śrī Rādhā, standing amidst Her sakhīs. [1]Crimson clouds of gulāl rise in all four directions, spreading such a hue that nothing remains clearly visible. Gentle laughter, playful teasing, lively gestures, and love-filled exchanges transform the entire atmosphere into sweetness itself. Śrī Nāgarīdāsa describes how the divine couple, Rādhā Kṛṣṇa, fill golden vessels with colors and pour them upon one another in loving sport, making this Holī truly unparalleled and wondrous. [2]

title: Shri Radha Bhajaniya Cha Tad Bhaktakanam - Shri Vanshi Ali, Sri Radha Siddhant (97)
sanskrit_text: Shri Radha Bhajaniya Cha Tad Bhaktakanam Cha Sangatih.Karya Manishibhir Nityam Iti Siddhanta Samsthiti. - Shri Vanshi Ali, Sri Radha Siddhant (97)One should worship Śrī Rādhā and constantly remain in the association of Her exclusive devotees. The truly wise follow this path every moment, for it firmly establishes unwavering devotion at the lotus feet of Kiśorī Jī — this is the conclusion of the spiritual doctrine.

title: Radha Naam Japo Din Raina - Shri Hita Gopal Das [Of Sewa Kunj], Nikunj Ras Vallari (72)
sanskrit_text: (Raag Malkosh, Tritaal)Radha Naam Japau Din Raina.Jo Koi Radha Naam Sunave, Tabahi Parai Hiy Chaina. [1]Shri Radha Gaun Radha Ladaun, Radha Sune Ye Baina.Radha Naam Raseelo Ratihon, Chhavi Aave Hiy Naina. [2]Ravi Tanaya Pyari Jab Dekhun, Bolun Kar Kar Sena.Hitgopal Shri Naam Ki Mahima, Kaise Kahat Banaina. [3]- Shri Hita Gopal Das [Of Sewa Kunj], Nikunj Ras Vallari (72)One should chant the holy name of Śrī Rādhā day and night. Only when this sacred name enters my ears does my heart find true peace and rest. [1]May I sing the glories of Śrī Rādhā at every moment, tenderly love Her, and offer all my prayers at Her lotus feet. The name “Rādhā” is filled with infinite divine rasa. By remembering this holy name, the enchanting form of Śrī Rādhā vividly manifests within my heart and before my eyes. [2]Whenever I behold the gentle stream of Śrī Yamunā, the daughter of the Sun, it feels as though she too is softly singing the sweet name of Rādhā. I bow to her again and again. Śrī Hitgopāl Dās declares that the glory of this sacred Rādhā-name cannot be fully expressed in words. [3]

title: Yasyah Sphurjatpadanakhamani Jyoti - Shri Hita Harivansh Mahaprabhu, Shri Radha Sudha Nidhi (72)
sanskrit_text: Yatpadamburuhek Renu-kanikan Mudhrna Nidhatun Na Hi Prapurabrahm Shivadayopyadhikrtin Gopyaik Bhavashrayah.Sapi Premasudha Rasambudhinidhi Radhapi Sadharani Bhuta Kalagatikramen Balina He Daiv Tubhyan Namah.- Shri Hita Harivansh Mahaprabhu, Shri Radha Sudha Nidhi (72)Even Brahmā, Śiva, and other gods, after taking shelter of the mood of the gopīs, could not obtain even a single particle of dust from Her lotus feet. Such a supreme Queen of love, Śrī Rādhā, the treasure of the great ocean of nectar, now appears like an ordinary gopī due to the powerful flow of time. O Destiny — I bow to you.

title: Gavat Pyaro Radha Tero Jasu -  Shri Hariram Vyas, Vyas Vani, Uttarardh (170)
sanskrit_text: (Rag Sarang)Gavat Pyaro Radha Tero Jasu.Teroi Naam Japat Aur Bilapatu Hai, Kaamkau Syamhin Sank Su. [1]Kahyo Na Parai Darun Dukh Pyari, Tere Virah Mohan Ke Kanth Rahyo Asu.Vyas Swamini Karunakari Rakhyo, Hari Chakhyo Adhar-Sudharasu. [2]- Shri Hariram Vyas, Vyas Vani, Uttarardh (170)Śrī Harirāma Vyāsa, absorbed in the mood of a confidential sakhī, offers a heartfelt prayer to Śrī Rādhā—O Śrī Rādhe! Your beloved Śrī Kṛṣṇa sings only Your glories without cease. He chants none but Your holy name and sheds tears heavily in the agony of separation.  Divine passion has so tormented Kṛṣṇa that he is utterly restless, wholly agitated in your devotion. [1]O Pyārī Jū! The unbearable anguish that Śrī Mohana suffers in Your absence cannot be expressed in words. His very life-breath has risen to His throat—such is the extremity of His viraha, as though He endures a death-like torment. Śrī Harirāma Vyāsa humbly pleads, “O my Svāminī Śrī Rādhe! Bestow Your merciful darśana upon Him now and preserve His life, so that Śrī Hari may once again taste the ‘adharāmṛta’ (nectar of Your lips).” [2]

title: Swarath Ko Sansar Sab Paramarath Ko Khol - Shri Kant Kishor, Kant Rasik Ji Ki Vani, Doha (7)
sanskrit_text: Swarath Kau Sansar Sab, Paramarath Kau Khol.Baat Karen Ras-Reeti Ki, Bheetar Bhandar Dol.- Shri Kant Kishor, Kant Rasik Ji Ki Vani, Doha (7)The entire world remains absorbed in fulfilling its own selfish desires, while what is called spirituality, welfare, or charity is often nothing more than a display. Grand words are spoken about divine love and sacred rasa, yet the inner heart holds no treasure at all.

title: Nav Kunj Sadan Main Aaj Rangili Hori - Shri Bhagwat Rasik Ki Vani, Ananyarasikabharan Granth (12.2)
sanskrit_text: Nav Kunj-Sadan Main Aaj Rangili Hori.It Syama, Ut Syam Manohar, Khelat Umang Na Thori. [1]Chhal-Bal Ghat Lagavat Mohan, Ang Bachavat Gori.Savadhan Dou Sughar Manohar, Apni-Apni Ori. [2]Kok-Kala Kal-Keli Paraspar, Joban Jor Kisori.Chatur Khilar Ladili Lalan, Tum Jin Janao Bhori. [3]Haha Karau, Parau Payan Ab, Na Chalihain Barjori.Bhagavat Rasik Udar Swamini, Daihain Sarbasu Chhori. [4]- Shri Bhagwat Rasik, Bhagwat Rasik Ki Vani, Ananyarasikabharan Granth (12.2)In the ever-new Nikunja palace, today a festival of colors, Holī, unfolds. On one side stands Śrī Kiśorījī, and on the other stands Śrī Śyāmasundara, firm and enthusiastic. [1]With playful mischief and gentle force, Śyāmasundara tries again and again to shower Her with colors, but Kiśorījī skillfully guards Her delicate form. These beautiful, enchanting Beloveds, Priyā Lāla, are equally alert and skillful on their respective sides. Neither can impose color upon the other. [2]A smiling sakhī then says, “O Lālajī, do not think our Lāḍilījī naive. She is eternally youthful and unmatched in these loving sports. However clever you may be, she will not be conquered through these clever strategies.” [3]Your cleverness and force will not prevail here. Adopt the means you have always embraced—plead before Her and bow at Her lotus feet humbly. Svāminījī is exceedingly gracious; the moment You do so, She will lovingly offer Herself unto You. [4]

title: Aasamho Charanrenujushamaham Syama - Shrimad Bhagwatam (10.47.61)
sanskrit_text: Aasamho Charanrenujushamaham Syama Vrindavane Kimapi Gulamlatoshdheenam.- Shrimad Bhagwatam  (10.47.61)Oh Lord, may I be blessed to take birth as a bush, creeper, or simple herb in Vṛndāvana, so that these gopīs bless me with the dust of their lotus feet.

title: Tum Jaan Ayogya Bisaro Mujhe - Braj Ke Sawaiya
sanskrit_text: (Sawaiya)Tum Jaan Ayogya Bisaro Mujhe, Par Main Na Tumhen Bisaraya Karun.Gunagaan Karun Tera Dhyan Karun, Tum Maan Karo Main Manaya Karun. [1]Tere Hi Pujariyon Ki Pad-Dhuri, Main Nitya Hi Shish Chadhaya Karun.Tere Bhakt Ki Bhakti Karun Main Sada, Tere Chahne Walon Ko Chaha Karun. [2]- Braj Ke SawaiyaO Kṛṣṇa, even if You consider me unworthy and choose to forget me, still bestow such grace upon me that I may never forget You. May I forever sing Your divine glories, meditate upon You without cease, and when You show loving sulk, may I gently and devotedly strive to appease You. [1]Make my heart so pure that I may daily put the sacred dust of Your devotees’ feet over my head lovingly. May I remain ever engaged in serving Your devotees, and may I constantly love those who love You selflessly. [2]

May I remain ever engaged in serving Your devotees, and may I constantly love those who love You selflessly. [2]

[1]Tere Hi Pujariyon Ki Pad-Dhuri, Main Nitya Hi Shish Chadhaya Karun.Tere Bhakt Ki Bhakti Karun Main Sada, Tere Chahne Walon Ko Chaha Karun. [2]- Braj Ke SawaiyaO Kṛṣṇa, even if You consider me unworthy and choose to forget me, still bestow such grace upon me that I may never forget You. May I forever sing Your divine glories, meditate upon You without cease, and when You show loving sulk, may I gently and devotedly strive to appease You. [1]Make my heart so pure that I may daily put the sacred dust of Your devotees’ feet over my head lovingly. title: Radhe Ju Ke Bhal Pe Bendi Ati Chhabi Dey - Braj Ke Dohe
sanskrit_text: Radhe Ju Ke Bhaal Pai, Vendi Ati Chhabi Dey.Maanau Phooli Ketaki, Bhamar Baas Tahan Ley.- Braj Ke DoheThe bindi adorning Rādhā’s forehead shines with exceptional beauty. It appears like a love-intoxicated bee gently relishing the sweet fragrance of a freshly blossomed ketakī flower.

title: Kunjmahal Mein Aaj Rang Hori - Shri Bani Thani Ji
sanskrit_text: (Raag Khammayachi)Kunjmahal Mein Aaj Rang Hori.Phag Khel Mein Banavaniki, Hvai Rahi Pat Gathjori. [1]Mudit Hvai Naari Gulaal Udaaven, Gaaven Gaari Duhun Ori.‘Rasikvihari’ Sundar Dulah, Dulahani Naval Kishori. [2]- Shri Bani Thani JiToday, in the bowers of the kuñja-mahal, a vibrant festival of Holī unfolds. Amidst the playful exchange of colors, a most beautiful union has arisen — the garments of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa are being lovingly tied together in a sacred knot of oneness. [1]The sakhīs, overflowing with joy, scatter clouds of gulāl into the air and sing sweet, love-laden Holī songs from both sides. In this divine festivity, the charming Śrī Kṛṣṇa appears as the bridegroom, and Śrī Rādhā shines resplendent as the bride. [2]

title: Chal Na Sakai Nij Thaur Tain Je Tan Hum Abhiram - Shri Rasnidhi
sanskrit_text: Chal Na Sakai Nij Thaur Tain, Je Tan Drum Abhiram.Tahan Aai Ras Varasivau, Lajim Tuhi Ghanasyam.- Shri RasnidhiO Cloud! Just as the trees stand helpless, unable to walk toward water, it is your duty to bring rain to them. Similarly, when a soul becomes tired of wandering through countless lives and fully surrenders, Lord Ghanshyam Himself draws near, shelters that soul, and showers it with divine nectarous grace.

title: Dhaike Jai Ji Jamuna Tire - Shri Chhit Swami Ji Ki Vani (164)
sanskrit_text: (Raag Ramkali)Dhaike Jai Ji Jamuna Tire.Taaki Mahima Ab Kahan Laun Baraniye, Jai Parasat Ati Prem Neere. [1]Nisidin Keli Karat Manmohan, Piya Lai Ju Bhakt Ki Sang Bheere.“Chheet Swami” Giridharan Shri Vitthal, In-Binu Neku Na Dharat Dheere. [2]- Shri Chhit Swami, Shri Chhit Swami Ji Ki Vani (164)Run swiftly to the banks of the Yamunā. How far can her glory ever be described? The very touch of her sacred waters drenches the heart in divine love. [1]There, day and night, Manmohana Śrī Kṛṣṇa performs sweet amorous pastimes with His beloved Śrī Rādhā, bestowing supreme rasa upon the devotees. Śrī Chīta Svāmī says — Giridhara Lāla and His devotees cannot remain peaceful even for a single moment without these Yamunā-bank pastimes. [2]

title: Swarathmula Asudh Tyon Sudh Swabhav Anukul - Shri Raskhan, Prem Vatika (41)
sanskrit_text: Swarathmool Asuddh Tyon, Suddh Swabhaav-Anukool.Naradadi Prastaar Kari, Kiyau Jaahi Ko Tool.- Shri Raskhan, Prem Vatika (41)That love which is mixed with selfish motive is called impure love; and that which is selfless, effortlessly performed solely for the happiness of the Beloved, is known as pure love. Nārada and other exalted sages have explained these two forms of love.

title: Radha Naam Son Chit Raanch - Shri Lalit Kishori, Abhilash Madhuri, Vinay (202)
sanskrit_text: (Raag Desa)  Radha Naam Son Chit Raanch.Radha Naam Rekh Suchi Ruchison Antas Kaagad Khaanch. [1]Radha Naam Ank Aabhooshan Bhooshit Kar Ang Naach.Radha Naam Likhi Paatuliya Lalit Kishori Vaanch. [2]- Shri Lalit Kishori, Abhilash Madhuri, Vinay (202)Let the mind be fully absorbed in the holy name “Śrī Rādhā.” With pure, loving intent, inscribe the name Rādhā upon the inner paper of your heart. [1]Adorn every limb with the sacred marks of Rādhā-nāma as your true ornaments, and dance in that divine bliss. Śrī Lalitā Kiśorī says that such a “pāṭuliyā”(notebook/letter) lovingly written with the name Rādhā is eagerly read by the divine couple, Śrī Śyāma-Śyāma, with great joy. [2]

title: Dhing Vilasgarh Dangarh, Aur Mangarh Naam - Shri Priyadas Ji, Rasik Mohini (23)
sanskrit_text: Dhing Vilas-garh Daan-garh, Aur Maan-garh Nam.Gaur Khata Unvati Ihan, Chatrik Vah Ghanshyam.- Shri Priyadas Ji, Rasik Mohini (23)In the divine līlā-places of Barsānā, such as Vilāsgarh, Dāngarh, and Māngarh, the love-laden clouds of fair-complexioned Śrī Rādhā are forever showering. There, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, like a chataka bird longing for that rain, constantly drinks the flowing stream of Her love-bliss.

title: Bihari Lal Bankare Ju Anokhe - Shri Kishori Ali Ji, Vinay Ke Pad (50)
sanskrit_text: Bihari Laal Baankare Ju Anokhe.Karat Naye-Naye Khyaal Kautuki, Bhooli Rahe Kaau Dhokhe? [1]Naana Rang Darasai Vipin Main, Sab Hi Ras Dai Pokhe.Ab Kyon Jaarati Birah Jarani Bali, Kishori, Roop Ras Tokhe. [2]- Shri Kishori Ali Ji, Vinay Ke Pad (50)Śrī Kiśorī Alī Jī humbly addresses Śrī Bihārī Jī—O Bihārī Jī, You are so extremely mischievous. While performing Your countless playful līlās, have You somehow forgotten me in playful deception? [1]You once nourished me in Vṛndāvan with incomparable rasa through endless loving pastimes. Why now, O Bihārī Jī, have You left me to burn in the fire of Your separation? [2]

title: Aath Pahar Sumiran Kare Bisare Na Chhin Ek - Shri Sahjobai
sanskrit_text: Aath Pahar Sumiran Kare, Bisare Na Chhin Ek.Ashtadash Aur Chaar Mein, Sahjo Yahi Vishes.- Shri SahjobaiOne should remember the Lord constantly throughout all eight quarters of the day, with every single breath, and not forget Him even for a moment. This alone is the essence of all the four Vedas, the eighteen Purāṇas, and all sacred scriptures.

title: Brahma Indra Kahain Ham - Braj Nidhi Granthawali, Braj Shringar (7)
sanskrit_text: (Kavitt)Brahma Indra Kahain Ham Chaahain Naahin Padavi Kau,Braj Ke Na Brichh Bhaye Baithe Ihaan Haarikai. [1]Barnat Hain Gopi Ham Haari Naahi Laal Sang,Maan Hiy Haari Rahe Vaar Man Maarikai. [2]Kahat Kuber Hote Braj Ke Bater Tau To,Ber-Ber Brajanidhi Rahat Nihaarikai. [3]Braj-Raj Mein Lotat Gopal Hain Karat Khyaal,Yahai Dekhi Haal Daarau Teerath Sabai Vaarikai. [4]- Shri Braj Nidhi Ji, Braj Nidhi Granthawali, Braj Shringar (7)Lord Brahmā and Indra say, “We do not desire the sovereignty of Brahmaloka or even the throne of heaven. If we could obtain the fortune of becoming even a single tree in Braj, we would remain there forever.” [1]The Gopīs say, “In Braj Dham, we have not been defeated, for by accepting Lāl (Śrī Kṛṣṇa) as our everything and offering ourselves entirely unto Him, we have attained victory in love.” [2]Kubera says, “If only I were a tiny bird in Braj, I would again and again behold this treasure of Braj, Śrī Rādhā Kṛṣṇa, without cease.” [3]Seeing Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa rolling in the dust of Braj, Sri Brajanidhi contemplates—upon this Braj-dhāma, endowed with such supreme glory, even all holy places could be offered in sacrifice. [4]

title: Mukh So Bhashe Ananyta - Shri Roop Rasik Devacharya, Vishisht Doha (30)
sanskrit_text: Mukh So Bhashe Ananyta, Tan Mein Rakhe Thonti.Thakur Ke Aage Dhare, Ujjavana Ki Aunthi.- Shri Roop Rasik Devacharya, Vishisht Doha (30)People speak of exclusive devotion—“I belong only to Thākurjī; God alone is mine!”—yet within themselves they tightly conceal their attachments behind closed lips. Before the Lord, they merely display a hollow show of purity, while the inner darkness and deceit remain unchanged; their minds stay attached to wealth, honor, status, and family ties.

title: Dharm Arth Phal Kaam Moksh Sab Dur Viraje - Shri Hit Kishori Lal, Radha Sudha Nidhi Stva (77)
sanskrit_text: (Chappay)Dharm Arth Phal Kaam Moksh Sab Door Virajen.Kaha Tin Ki Batran Vritha Kijai Bin Kajen. [1]Hari Ki Bhakti Ananya Maha Padavi Kahi Gai.Sir Mathe Pai Rahau Kahau Pai Nij Man Bhai. [2]Adbhut Naval Kishori Mani Vasat Kunj Vrindavipin.Ruchat Na Mero Man Kahoon Jasu Rasamritdasya Bin. [3]- Shri Hit Kishori Lal, Radha Sudha Nidhi Stva (77)Let the four revered pursuits of life—Dharma, Artha, Kāma, and Mokṣa—remain honored in the world for those who aspire to them; I have no inclination even to speak of them. [1]Let the supreme attainment of exclusive devotion to Śrī Hari also be held dear by devotees; we offer it reverence, yet it is not our path. Those whose hearts are drawn to it may glorify it. [2]Our hearts, however, are satisfied only by the nectar of servitude to the wondrous, jewel-like Kiśorī, Śrī Rādhā, who eternally resides within the sacred realm of Śrī Vṛndāvan. [3]

[1]Hari Ki Bhakti Ananya Maha Padavi Kahi Gai.Sir Mathe Pai Rahau Kahau Pai Nij Man Bhai. [2]Adbhut Naval Kishori Mani Vasat Kunj Vrindavipin.Ruchat Na Mero Man Kahoon Jasu Rasamritdasya Bin. [3]- Shri Hit Kishori Lal, Radha Sudha Nidhi Stva (77)Let the four revered pursuits of life—Dharma, Artha, Kāma, and Mokṣa—remain honored in the world for those who aspire to them; I have no inclination even to speak of them. [1]Let the supreme attainment of exclusive devotion to Śrī Hari also be held dear by devotees; we offer it reverence, yet it is not our path. Those whose hearts are drawn to it may glorify it. [2]Our hearts, however, are satisfied only by the nectar of servitude to the wondrous, jewel-like Kiśorī, Śrī Rādhā, who eternally resides within the sacred realm of Śrī Vṛndāvan. [3]
author: Braj Rasik Heritage

title: Anvar Kanvar Jo Jure Rukho Utam Bhog - Shri Hita Damodar Das, Nem Battisi (19)
sanskrit_text: Anvar Kanvar Jo Jurai, Rukhau Uttam Bhog.Vrindavan Pari Rahau, Dukh Sukh Kuch Sanjog.- Shri Hita Damodar Das, Nem Battisi (19)Whether one has garments to wear or blankets for warmth, whether one is given rich food, simple fare, or nothing at all, and whatever joys or sorrows may arise, in whatever condition life unfolds, to reside always in Śrī Vṛndāvan alone is life’s highest fulfillment and truest perfection.

title: Ras Matt Biharini Pyari Hai - Shri Lalit Kishori Dev Ju Ki Vani, Shringar Ras Ke Pad (69)
sanskrit_text: Rasa Matt Biharini Pyari Hai.Nenk Lakhen Bas Bhaye Ladile, Adbhut Roop Ujyari Hai. [1]Umgyau Rang Sarovar Hiy Mein, Mridu Muskan Kachu Nyari Hai.Shri Haridasi Ke Hit Viharat, Jeevani Praan Hamari Hai. [2]- Shri Lalit Kishori Dev, Shri Lalit Kishori Dev Ju Ki Vani, Shringar Ras Ke Pad (69)Śrī Kuñjabihārinī (Śrī Rādhā) remains ever intoxicated in the nectar of love. Her form is endowed with unparalleled radiance. Merely a slight glance enslaves Śrī Kṛṣṇa under Her control. [1]Such enchantment dwells in her gentle smile that a lake of love-nectar begins to surge within the heart. The whole treasure of our life, Śyāmā Pyārī, eternally engages in love-plays of nitya vihāra only to bestow nectar upon Her intimate sakhīs such as Lalitā Haridāsī Jī. [2]

title: Piya Pyari Nij Keli Main - Shri Roop Sakhi, Shringar Rasa Ke Dohe (15)
sanskrit_text: Piya Pyari Nij Keli Main, Tan Man Mili Abhiram.Ang Ang Sobha Saras, Kunj Mahal Nij Dham.- Shri Roop Sakhi, Shringar Rasa Ke Dohe (15)Absorbed in Their intimate kelī, the divine couple, Priyā–Priyatam, appear irresistibly enchanting as They become one in body and mind. The sweetness of each of Their limbs shines beautifully, and the kuñja-mahal serves as the hidden abode of Their love-filled pastimes.

title: Vrajleela Ras Bhave Ab To - Shri Yugal Priya
sanskrit_text: (Raag Peelu - Taal Kaharva)Vrajleela Ras Bhaavai Ab To,Shrigiriraaj Ank Mein Rahiye. [1]Kariye Binay Nihori Bhaanti Bahu, Syamroop Mridu Madhuri Lahiye. [2] Chaliye Sang Rasik Bhaktanke,Prem Prabaah Magan Hvai Bahiye. [3] Gaay Gubind Naam Gun Keertan,Janam Janamke Tahn Dukh Dahiye. [4]Kariye Kaalindi Jal Majjan,Nit Madhukari Lai Nirabahiye. [5] Jugalpriya Preetam Bhuj Bharikai,Paiy Jo Kachhu Chahiye. [6]- Shri Yugal PriyaNow nothing feels pleasing to me apart from the divine līlās of Braj. Supreme perfection of life lies in residing in the sacred foothills of Girirāj Ji alone. [1]With humble prayers offered at the lotus feet of Śrī Girirāj Jī, one is blessed with the darshan of Śrī Śyāmsundara’s supremely sweet form. [2]Always remain in the association of rasik devotees, for from their presence flows the river of divine love, naturally carrying the soul into blissful absorption. [3]By chanting Govinda’s holy names and glories, the grief accumulated over innumerable lifetimes is reduced to ashes. [4]Daily bathe in the sacred waters of Śrī Yamunā Jī and, sustaining life through madhukarī, dwell in holy detachment. [5]Śrī Yugala-priyā Jī says, “Hold your beloved Śrī Kṛṣṇa close in your arms and fulfill the deepest desires of your heart.” [6]

title: Taadatterpitvastuni Radhasanketmantara - Shri Vagish Shastri Ji, Shri Radha Saptashati (1.45)
sanskrit_text: Taadatterpitvastuni Radhasanketmantara.Kevalasya Cha Krishnasya Doshayaradhanam Matam.- Shri Vagish Shastri Ji, Shri Radha Saptashati (1.45)Śrī Kṛṣṇa does not accept offerings without Śrī Rādhā’s approval. Worshipping Śrī Kṛṣṇa alone, without Śrī Rādhā, is considered incomplete and spiritually faulty.

title: Vrishabhanu Kunvari Khelati Basant - Shri Krishndas, Shri Krishndas Adhikari Ji Ki Vani (961)
sanskrit_text: (Raag Basant)Vrishabhanu Kunvari Khelati Basant, Phooli Sakhi Jahan Naval Kant.Taal Mridang Bajai Aru Nisan, Khelan Nikasin Sukhnidhan. [1]Choba Kunkum Machi Hai Keech, Mrigamad Sakhi Javadi Beech.Saghan Kunj Mein Sukh-Tarang, Krishnadas Aali Radhe Ravan-Sang. [2]- Shri Krishndas, Shri Krishndas Adhikari Ji Ki Vani (961)Śrī Vṛṣabhānu’s charming daughter, Śrī Rādhā, is engaged in the plays of the spring season, where Her ever-new beloved Śyāmasundara is also present. The sakhīs have blossomed with joy. The sounds of drums, cymbals, and kettledrums resonate through the air, while Śrī Rādhā Mahārānī, the very mine of bliss, has stepped out from her palace to engage in the festivities. [1]Colored powders and fragrant paste of saffron powder and vermilion powder have transformed sand into crimson mud, while the sakhīs revel amidst the fragrance of musk and fine perfumes. In the dense bowers, waves of nectar arise. Śrī Kṛṣṇadāsa says that, together with her lovely companions, Śrī Rādhā is relishing the spring līlā in the company of Śrī Kṛṣṇa. [2]

title: Karo Kripa Sri Radhika - Shri Hanuman Prasad Poddar (Bhaiji), Pad Ratnakar, Vandana Evam Prarthna (15.1)
sanskrit_text: Karo Kripa Sri Radhika, Binavon Barambar.Bani Rahe Smriti Madhur-Suchi, Mangalmay Sukhsar. - Shri Hanuman Prasad Poddar (Bhaiji), Pad Ratnakar, Vandana Evam Prarthna (15.1)O most merciful Śrī Rādhikā, I earnestly beg for Your grace. Repeatedly, I bow with this gentle prayer, that Your supremely pure and charming form may always reside within my mind, for it is all-auspicious and the very source of divine bliss.

title: Nek Aage Aa Shyam Tope Rang Daaron - Shri Chandrasakhi Ji
sanskrit_text: Nek Aage Aa Shyam Tope Rang Daaron.Abeer Gulaal Malo Mukh Tere, Gaalan Par Gulcha Maaron. [1]Choba Chandan Aur Aragaja, Kanak Katoran Bhari Dhaaron.‘Chandrasakhi’ Bhaj Balakrishna Chhavi, Tan Man Dhan Tope Vaaron. [2]- Shri Chandrasakhi JiO Śyāmasundara, come a little closer so I may sprinkle colors upon You. I will anoint your face with abīra (scented powders) and red gulāla, and give your cheeks a playful, loving tap. [1]I will pour fragrant sandalwood powder and aragajā (aromatic paste) over you again and again from golden bowls. Śrī Candrasakhī says that by the grace of her Gurudev Śrī Hita Bālakṛṣṇa Ji, she offers her body, mind, and wealth entirely unto You. [2]

title: Braj Vrindavan Aghat Rasa Radha Krishna Sarupa - Braj Ke Dohe
sanskrit_text: Braj-Vrindavan Aghat Ras, Radha Krishna Saroop.Naam Let Paatak Katai, Jyon Harinaam Anoop.- Braj Ke DoheBraj Vṛndāvan is filled with unparalleled divine rasa, which is the very embodiment of Śrī Rādhā–Kṛṣṇa Themselves. Merely uttering the names of their sacred pastime places destroys sins. Their glory is incomparable, equal to the supreme glory of Śrī Harinām.

title: Hori Aai Ri Rang Rangeeli - Shri Kishoridas (of Gaudiya sect.)
sanskrit_text: Hori Aai Ri Rang Rangeeli Chhabeeli Man Bhaai.Nav Pallav Kusumit Vrindaban Madhup Gunj Sukhdaai. [1]Vaajan Lage Dhaf Aur Murali, Bolan Kokil Lagat Suhaai.Shri Brajchandra Kishori Manvanchhit Vraj Par Phag Ghumaai. [2]- Shri Kishoridas (Of Gaudiya Sect.)The colorful festival of Holī, which delights everyone’s heart, has arrived. The humming of bumblebees, amidst fresh leaves and blossoms in Śrī Dhām Vṛndāvan, appears utterly mesmerizing. [1]The ḍhaph drum and flute have begun to sound, and the cuckoo’s song feels pleasant. Śrī Brajachandra (Kṛṣṇa) and Kishorī (Rādhā), following their own sweet will, joyfully play Holī and immerse all of Braj in their divine colors. [2]

title: Shri Vrindavan Ke Vriksh Ko Maram Na Jaane Koy - Goswami Shri Hariray Ji, Vallabh Saakhi (73)
sanskrit_text: Shri Vrindavan Ke Vriksh Ko, Maram Na Jaane Koy.Ek Paat Ko Sumar Ke, Aap Chaturbhuj Hoy.- Goswami Shri Hariray Ji, Vallabh Saakhi (73)No one can truly comprehend the mystery of the trees of Śrī Vṛndāvan. Simply remembering even a single leaf of these trees grants one divine strength like that of the Lord’s four-armed form, for Śrī Kṛṣṇa personally resides in every tree and every leaf here.

Simply remembering even a single leaf of these trees grants one divine strength like that of the Lord’s four-armed form, for Śrī Kṛṣṇa personally resides in every tree and every leaf here.
author: Braj Rasik Heritage

title: Aaj Sakhi Doun Kunj Bihari - Shri Dayabai
sanskrit_text: Aaj Sakhi Doun Kunj Bihari.Auchak Aay Mile Kunjan Mein, Laal Laadili Pyaari. [1]Gaur Shyam Shobha Ke Sagar, Ang-Ang Ki Chhavi Nyaari.Nirakhat Roop Seetal Bhaye Naina, Ur Anand Apaari. [2]Safal Manorath Bhaye Sab Man Ke, Virah Bitha Sab Taari.‘Daya’ Kunwari Daasi Nij Kini, Charan Kamal Par Vaari. [3]- Shri DayabaiSeeing her intense longing for God realization, Śrī Dayābāī Jī was instructed by her Gurudeva, Śrī Caraṇdās Jī, to reside in Vṛndāvan. The vision of Śyāmā–Śyām that she received there is described as follows—O friend! Today, the two Kuñja-Bihārīs (Śrī Lāḍilī-Lāl) suddenly met me within the secluded forest bower. [1]Fair and dark in complexion, Śyāmā-Kuñja-Bihārī are oceans of beauty. The splendor of each of their limbs is utterly unique. Beholding their form, the eyes became cooled, and the heart filled with boundless bliss. [2]All the desires of my heart were fulfilled, and every pain of separation vanished. Śrī Dayābāī says, “Sri Rādhā made me Her own maidservant; I offer myself completely at Their lotus feet.” [3]

title: Bhalein Karo Jap Yog Tap - Shri Lalit Ladaiti, Shri Kishori Kripa Kataksha, Madhurya Ras Dohavali (106)
sanskrit_text: Bhalein Karo Jap Yog Tap, Daan Dharm Vrat Nem.‘Lalit Ladaiti’ Prem Bin, Swapane Kushal Na Kshem.- Shri Lalit Ladaiti, Shri Kishori Kripa Kataksha, Madhurya Ras Dohavali (106)Even if a person remains constantly engaged in japa, yoga, austerities, charity, religious duties, vows, and disciplines, if the mind is devoid of God’s love, then true welfare, inner peace, and contentment cannot be attained — not even in a dream.

title: Bhare Drig Vari Uchchar Van Prem San - Sri Albeli Ali, Vrindavansata (24)
sanskrit_text: (Kavitt)Bharai Drig Vari Uchchar Van Prem Saun,Poorn Soi Preeti Kab Hoi Man Ki. [1]Shaan Aur Paan Sukh Sain Jo Na Mile,Daiv-Gati Hoi Jo Hasi Tan Ki. [2]Vivas Hvai Jai Ang-Ang Sat Took Jo,Tajat Nahin Soor Jyon Bhoomi Ran Ki. [3]Hohi Tan Chheen Dushleen Jo Koti Vidhi,Albeli Jin Jaav Raj Chhaandi Ban Ki. [4]- Sri Albeli Ali, Vrindavansata (24)O Śrī Rādhā Rāṇī! While dwelling in Śrī Vṛndāvan, when will that blessed moment come when streams of tears will flow from my eyes in Your love, and I shall chant Your holy name lovingly? When will such pure and selfless love awaken within my heart? [1]Let honor be lost, let food and rest not come—there is no sorrow in that, even if destiny makes this body suffer. [2]Even if this body were torn apart piece by piece, still I would not leave Vṛndāvan, just as a brave warrior never leaves the battlefield. [3]Even if the body becomes deficient and countless troubles come together, Alabelī Ali still never wishes to abandon the dust of holy Vṛndāvan. [4]

title: Ratan Jatan Anso Karo Satan Karo Banvas - Shri Kishori Ali (Letter to Ratan Ali)
sanskrit_text: Ratan Jatan Anso Karo, Satan Karon Banvaas.Latan-Latan Tari Nain Bhari, Nirakho Bibidh Bilas.- Shri Kishori Ali (Letter to Ratan Ali)Give up worldly pleasures and make such an effort that you may attain residence in Śrī Dhām Vṛndāvan, the capital city of rasik devotees, in the association of rasikas. Then, there among the vines and leaves, behold the divine plays of love of the divine couple, Śrī Śyāmā–Śyām.

title: Darsan Dai Nikasi Ata Mein Te - Sri Purushottam Ji
sanskrit_text: Darsan Dai Nikasi Ata Mein Te.Lat Sarakay Dars Dai Pyari, Nikasyo Chand Ghata Mein Te. [1]Koti Rama Savitri Bhavani, Nikasi Charan Chhata Mein Te. Purushottam Prabhu Yah Ras Chakhyo, Makhan Kadhyo Matha Mein Te. [2]- Sri Purushottam JiŚrī Puruṣottam Ji, while describing the beautiful form of Śrī Rādhā and humbly yearning for Her darśan, says —When Śrī Rādhikā steps out upon the high terrace and bestows Her darśan, gently moving aside Her dark locks to unveil Her face, it seems like the full moon rising from behind a veil of clouds. [1]From the radiance of Her lotus feet, it seems as though countless Lakṣmīs, Sāvitrīs, and Bhavānīs manifest on the spot. Puruṣottam Ji says that the taste of this divine rasa is like freshly churned butter drawn out from buttermilk. [2]

title: Lalit Phagu Rachna Rachi - Shri Ghananand Ji, Ghananand Granthawali, Saras Vasant (66)
sanskrit_text: Lalit Phagu Rachna Rachi, Bilasat Saras Basant.Jai Jai Radha Madhavi, Jai Banmali Kant.- Shri Ghananand Ji, Ghananand Granthawali, Saras Vasant (66)A supremely enchanting celebration of Phāg (the playful Holī) has been beautifully arranged, and the sweet spring season shines forth in full delight. All glories to Śrī Rādhā Jū, the beloved of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, and all glories to Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the garland-wearing Lord of the forest.

title: Chalo Lal Khelen Basant Mili - Shri Narayan Swami, Braj Vihar, Vasant Leela (15)
sanskrit_text: (Raga Vasant Dheematal)Chalo Lal Khelen Vasant Mili Shri Yamuna Ke Kula.Nav Nikunj Van Nai Ritu Aai Naye Naye Phoole Phula. [1]Drum Daarin Baithe Nav Pakshi Bolat Ati Anukula.‘Narayan’ Ut Nai Bahar Sukh, Itmen Tum Sukh Mula. [2]- Sri Narayan Swami, Braj Vihar, Vasant Leela (15)Kiśorī Jī (Śrī Rādhā) says to Lāl Jī (Śrī Kṛṣṇa): O Beloved! Come, let us go and play vasanta (spring) season plays together on the banks of Śrī Yamunā. In the forest bowers, the new season has arrived, and fresh flowers have blossomed everywhere. [1]On the branches of the trees, new birds sit and sing in sweet and pleasing tones. Śrī Nārāyaṇ Swāmī says—there, the joy of the new spring thrives, but here, You are the very source of all joy. [2]

title: Koti-Koti Rasana Jo Rom - Shri Hita Dhruvdas, Bayalees Leela, Shringar Sabha Mandal (126)
sanskrit_text: Roop Priya Ko Kahan Ko, Kitaki Budhi Hai Mor.Tei Kunwar Charanani Luthat, Nirakhi Nain Ki Kor.- Shri Hita Dhruvdas, Bayalees Leela, Shringar Sabha Mandal (39)How could my limited intellect ever have the power to describe the divine beauty of Śrī Priyājī (Śrī Rādhā)? With just a single glance from the corner of Her eyes, even the Supreme Lord, Śrī Kṛṣṇa Himself, becomes enchanted and, overwhelmed in divine ecstasy, rolls at Her lotus feet.

title: Khelat Hain Vasant Vihari Viharin - Goswami Shri Hitalal Ji
sanskrit_text: Khelat Hain Vasant Vihari Viharin.Abeer Gulaal Ghumad Ras Ambud, Jhar Laayau Manu Rang Pichkarin. [1]Madhur Garaj Baajenu Dhuni Manu Pik, Mor Kuhuk Ho-Ho Kilkarin.Jai Shri Hitlal Prem Ur Bheejan, Hansat Hansavat Dai Kartarin. [2]- Goswami Shri Hitalal JiThe Divine Couple, Śrī Vihārī–Vihārin, are celebrating the festival of spring today. Clouds of abīra and gulāla surge like showers of color, as if syringes of hues are raining down the very colors of love. [1]Sweet music resounds—the cuckoo’s song, the peacock’s call, and bursts of laughter with sounds “Ho Ho Hori Hai” fill the atmosphere. Śrī Hitlāl says—they soak hearts in love, laughing and making others laugh as they perform this divine play. [2]

title: Nitt Sarad Nitt Teej Hai - Shri Lalit Kishori Dev Ju Ki Vani, Vishistha Pada & Saakhi (1185)
sanskrit_text: Nitt Sarad Nitt Teej Hai, Nitt Hori Su Basant.Nitt Keli Chhin Chhin Nai, Jaake Sukhahi Na Ant.- Shri Lalit Kishori Dev, Shri Lalit Kishori Dev Ju Ki Vani, Vishistha Pada & Saakhi (1185)Where the autumn season is ever-present, where the festival of Tīj is celebrated eternally, and where the joy of spring and Holī is forever experienced; where at every moment the Divine Couple performs ever-new plays of love, whose bliss knows no end—that alone is the eternal abode of Śrī Vṛndāvan.

title: Hamare Yahan Ke Sadhu Prasad Na Chahe -  Shri Lalit Mohini Dev Ju Ki Vani, Siddhant Ke Pad (13)
sanskrit_text: Hamare Yahan Ke Sadhu Prasada Na Chahen. Na Vastra Ko Adanga Lagaven. [1]Magana Bhaye Guna Gaven. Priyacharana China-China Saharavain. [2]Basi Vrindavan Anata Na Javein. Lalitamohini Tinhe Ladaavein. [3]-  Shri Lalit Mohini Dev, Shri Lalit Mohini Dev Ju Ki Vani, Siddhant Ke Pad (13)The saints of our lineage, followers of Śrī Svāmī Haridās Jī, do not prefer to accept prasād from any deity except Śrī Priya-Priyatam, nor do they pay heed to special clothing or other outward formalities. [1]Absorbed in divine bliss, they ceaselessly sing the glories of the divine couple and worship the lotus feet of Śrī Priyājī (Śrī Rādhā), every moment. [2]They dwell exclusively in Śrī Vṛndāvana and do not go elsewhere. Such rare and fortunate rasik devotees are forever dear to me, says Śrī Lalitmohinī. [3]

title: Shri Vrindavan Teri Jai Hove - Shri Radhacharan Das, Vrindavan Virudavali (35)
sanskrit_text: Shri Vrindavan Teri Jai Hove.He Karuna Dhan Rasikan Jeevan Rasamay Kanan Jai Hove. [1]He Abhayankar Param Shubhankar Yugal Priyankar Jai Hove.Hridaya Dharohar Param Manohar Mahamodkar Jai Hove. [2]Param Prabhakar Prem Sudhakar Ras Ratnakar Jai Hove.Radha Charan Das Hriday Dhan Jai Hove Teri Jai Hove. [3]- Shri Radhacharan Das, Vrindavan Virudavali (35)O Śrī Vṛndāvan Dhām, all glories to you. You are an unfathomable ocean of compassion, the very life-breath of rasik devotees, and a divine forest overflowing with rasa-filled līlās—all glory to you. You are the priceless treasure of devotees’ hearts, exceedingly enchanting and the bestower of incomparable bliss. [2]You are the supreme embodiment of divine light, endlessly showering the nectar of love, and an inexhaustible mine of rasa. You are the entire wealth of the heart of Śrī Rādhācaraṇ Dās—O Śrī Vṛndāvan, endless glories to You! [3]

title: Kab Lotun Ati Vikal Hvai Vraj-Raj mahan Harshay - Shri Prabhudutt Brahmachari, Sri Vrindavan Mahatmya (3)
sanskrit_text: Kab Lotun Ati Vikal Hvai, Vraj-Rajmahan Harshaay.Karu Keech Kab Dhuriki, Nayanan Neer Bahay.- Shri Prabhudutt Brahmachari, Sri Vrindavan Mahatmya (3)When will I, utterly restless in longing, joyfully roll in the dust of Vraja? When will I moisten that sacred dust with my own tears, turning it into a mire of love as streams of loving tears flow from my eyes?

title: Jab Prem Ke Panth Mein Pair Diya - Dandi Swami Shri Hare Krishnanand Sarasvati
sanskrit_text: (Sawaiya)Jab Prem Ke Panth Mein Pair Diya, Tab Kya Uske Dukh Se Darna Hai.Jal Bhojan Ki Mat Chaah Karo, Talvaar Tale Shir Ko Dharna Hai. [1]Bas Yaad Mein Rote Huye Unki, Nij Praan Visarjan Bhi Karna Hai.Vah Aasha Niraasha Liye Apni, Kabhi Jeena Hai Mitra. Kabhi Marna Hai. [2]- Dandi Swami Shri Hare Krishnanand Sarasvati ‘Hare Krishn’Once one steps onto the path of love, why  fear the sorrows encountered along it? On this path, even the desire for water and food is to be abandoned, and one must walk forward without hesitation, placing one’s head willingly beneath the sword. [1]Shedding tears incessantly in remembrance of the Beloved, one must be ready to offer one’s very life in complete self-surrender. Bearing both hope and despair within your heart, O friend—sometimes you must live, and sometimes you must be prepared to die. [2]

title: Sab Ras Kau Ras Prem Hai Vishayi Khele Saar - Sri Surdas, Soor Sagar
sanskrit_text: Sab Ras Kau Ras Prem Hai, Vishayi Khele Saar.Tan-Man-Dhan-Jauban Khase, Tau Na Mane Haar.- Sri Surdas, Soor Sagar (325.11)Among all nectars in this world, the supreme and highest is prema-rasa, the rasa of divine love. The gambler stakes everything—body, mind, wealth, youth—losing all in the play, yet he never accepts defeat. In the same way, one who enters the play of love surrenders everything into it, unwilling to turn back, for love itself becomes his sole victory.

title: Man Pachhitaihai Avsar Bite - Shri Tulsidas
sanskrit_text: Man Pachhitaihai Avasar Beete.Durlabh Deh Pai Haripad Bhaju, Karam, Bachan Aru Heete. [1]Sahasbaahu, Dasbadan Aadi Nrip, Bache Na Kaal Baleete.Ham Ham Kari Dhan Dhaam Sanvaare, Ant Chale Uthi Reete. [2]Sut Banitaadi Jaani Svaarath Rat, Na Karu Neh Sabheete.Antahu Tohin Tajenge Paamar! Too Na Tajai Abheete. [3]Ab Naathahin Anuraagu Jaagu Jad, Tyaagu Duraasa Jeete.Bujhai Na Kaam Agini Tulasi Kahen, Vishaybhog Bahu Ghee Te. [4]- Shri Tulsidas O mind! If this golden opportunity slips away, in the end you will do nothing except regret. You have attained this rare human birth, therefore, worship the lotus feet of Śrī Hari with exclusive devotion through action, speech, and heart. [1]Even mighty kings like Sahasrabāhu and Rāvaṇa could not save themselves from the fierce force of God of death. Lost in the pride of “I” and “mine,” they adorned wealth, splendor, and palaces—yet in the end they abandoned everything and departed empty-handed. [2]Do not become entangled in the web of selfish attachment by considering son, wife, and relatives alone as your own. O foolish mind! In the end they will all forsake you—so why not renounce their delusion now itself? [3]O incautious mind! Now awaken love for the supremely compassionate Lord and abandon vain hopes. Śrī Tulasīdāsa says—sense enjoyments do not extinguish the fire of desire; rather, they pour ghee into it and make it blaze all the more fiercely. [4]

title: Thakurai Pyari Lai Sevkaai Pi Vant - Shri Lalit Kishori, Abhilash Madhuri, Phutkar Pad (69)
sanskrit_text: Thakuraai Pyaari Lai, Sivkaai Pi Vaant.Preeti Reeti Yak Saar Sakhi, Dai Manon Yak Saant.- Shri Lalit Kishori, Abhilash Madhuri, Phutkar Pad (69)In divine rasa of Vrindavan, Rādhā assumed lordship, Kṛṣṇa took servitude. Both surrendered their hearts and their entire being to one another, so completely that their minds became one. O friend, is the supreme secret of the prem-rīti (mode of love).

title: Kaindho Raskhan Ras Kos - Shri Raskhan, Raskhan Ratnavali
sanskrit_text: (Kavitta)Kaindho Rasakhana Rasa Kosa Drriga Pyasa Jani,Ani Ke Piyusha Pusha Kino Bidhi Chamda Ghara. [1] Kaindho Mani Manika Baitharibai Ko Kamchana Maim,Jariya Jobana Jina Gadaiya Sughara Ghara. [2]Kaindho Kama Kamana Ke Rajata Adhara Chinha,Kaindho Yaha Bhaura Gyan Bohita Gumana Hara. [3]Eri Meri Pyari Duti Koti Rati Rambha Ki,Vari Daron Tehi Chita Chorani Chibuka Para. [4]- Shri Raskhan, Raskhan RatnawaliDescribing the beauty of Śrī Rādhā, Raskhān says—Brahmā, knowing the world to be thirsty, filled Your eyes with an inexhaustible treasure of bliss so that the world might be fully satisfied. Your face appears as if the moon of the essence of nectar has assumed a personal form. [1]The graceful formation of Your limbs is as though a master jeweler, perfected in his art, has fashioned an incomparable abode of youth, setting gems and pearls into gold, each limb complete and flawless in its own splendor. [2]The crimson hue of Your lips is so enchanting that it seems the entire kingdom of Kāma resides within them, and this beauty, like a bumblebee, shatters the pride of the boat of knowledge, causing it to sink. [3]O my lovely Rādhā! Upon the beauty of Your charming chin, I would gladly sacrifice millions of Ratis and Rambhās, for such unparalleled beauty is found nowhere else. [4]

title: Niraye Sthiti Revastu Na Syat - Shri Vanshi Ali, Sri Radha Siddhant (101)
sanskrit_text: Niraye Sthiti Revastu Na Syat Parapade Gatih.Yatra Tatra Janirvarstu Masturadha Padachyutih.- Shri Vanshi Ali, Sri Radha Siddhant (101)Even if I am cast into hell, even if I never reach the supreme abode; even if I wander through countless births in any realm whatsoever—may I never, even for a moment, turn away from exclusive devotion to the lotus feet of Śrī Rādhā, nor from the loving service of those divine feet.

title: Pyare Teri Vanshi Radha-Radha Bole - Shri Priyadas
sanskrit_text: Pyare Teri Vanshi Radha-Radha Bole.Radha Roop Dikhaai Aapano, Binahu Mol Liyau Mole. [1]Vanshi-Vanshi Kari Dampati Ke, Prem-Manjoosha Khole.‘Priyasakhi’ Radha Suni Mohan, Gohan Laagyo Dole. [2]- Shri Priyadas JiO beloved! Your flute continually sings the sweet name of “Rādhā, Rādhā.” Through its melody, it reveals the very form of Śrī Rādhā and, without demanding any price, steals the hearts of all. [1]Through the notes of the flute, the priceless treasure of the divine couple’s love is revealed. Śrī Priyāsakhī says—the moment the name of Śrī Rādhā reaches the ears of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, His heart begins to sway in a flood of divine love. [2]

sanskrit_text: Ram Inhai Sab Kahat Hain, Taako Arth Rasaal. Ra Akshar Shriradhika, Ma Manmohan Laal.- Sri Ramsakhiji, Shri Bhaktiras ManjariThe name spoken by all as “Rāma” overflows with the supreme essence of divine rasa in the vision of rasika devotees. title: Radhekrishn Radhekrishn Radhekrishn Bol Re - Shri Roop Madhuri Ji Ki Vani, Padavali (47)
sanskrit_text: (Raag Prabhati)Radhekrishn Radhekrishn Radhekrishn Bol Re.Jagat Baad Son Maun Ley Mukh, Hari Characha Mein Kholre. [1]Svans Svans Hari Naam Sumir Le, Manush Janam Anamol Re.Bhakti Vidya Padho Manush Tan, Nahin Rahoge Tol Re. [2]Guru Sharan Mein Mauj Karo Nit, Aan Thaur Mat Dol Re."Roopmadhuri” Naam Sharkara, Prem Dugdh Pee Ghol Re. [3]- Shri Roop Madhuri, Shri Roop Madhuri Ji Ki Vani, Padavali (47)Chant the name of Rādhe–Kṛṣṇa constantly. Keep silent towards worldly talks, and open your mouth only to sing glories of Hari. [1]With every breath, remember the Name of Hari, for this human birth is exceedingly precious. Study the wisdom of devotion in this human body, and your life will not go in vain. [2]Live joyfully in the shelter of the Guru and do not wander elsewhere. Rūpamādhurī says—dissolve the sugar of the Holy Name in the milk of love, and drink it fully. [3]

title: Aiso Barsanao Nirkhi Gahbar Aayo Prem - Shri Nagridas Ji Ki Vani, Tirthanand (28)
sanskrit_text: Aiso Barsaanao Nirkhi, Gahbar Aayo Prem.Karat Dandavat Lutata Raj, Chhuti Gaye Raajas Nem.- Shri Nagridas Ji (Maharaj Sawant Singh), Shri Nagridas Ji Ki Vani, Tirthanand (28)Beholding such divine sights of Barsānā and gazing upon the sacred Gahvar Van, waves of love surged within the heart. title: Dhan Dhan Vrindavipin Papiha Pyare - Shri Abhay Ram, Vrindavan Rahasya Vinod (69)
sanskrit_text: Dhan Dhan Vrindavipin Papiha Pyare.Aur Neer Kau Peevat Naahin, Swati Boond Ke Paare. [1]Baarah Maas Pyaas Ko Paamein, Jinke Hari Rakhvaare.Abhayraam Ye Ha Badbhaagi, Raj Mein Rahein Vichaare. [2]- Shri Abhay Ram, Vrindavan Rahasya Vinod (69)Truly blessed are the papīhās (hawk cuckoo) of Vṛndāvan. They drink no other water and wait exclusively for the raindrops from the Svātī star. [1]Śrī Hari Himself satisfies their yearlong longing. Śrī Abhayarām says—most auspicious is the fate of that papīhā who lives in Vṛndāvan’s sacred dust. [2]

title: Nam Radhika Ke Sunat Hit Saun Mohanlal - Shri Hita Parmanand Das
sanskrit_text: Naam Radhika Ke Sunat, Hita Saun Mohanlaal.Subas Hoi Sukh Det Hain, 'Parmanand' Kripal.- Shri Hita Parmanand DasŚrī Kṛṣṇa listens to the name of Śrī Rādhikā with the utmost love. Enchanted by the power of the name “Rādhā,” Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who is the very embodiment of supreme bliss, becomes merciful toward the soul and bestows divine happiness upon it.

title: Bainu Mai Baaje Bansivat - Shri Hita Harivansh Mahaprabhu, Shri Hit Chaurasi (64)
sanskrit_text: (Raag Gauri)Bainu Maai Baajai Bansivat.Sada Basant Rahat Vrindavan Pulin Pavitra Subhag Yamuna Tat. [1]Jatit Kreet Makarakrit Kundal Mukhaarvind Bhanvar Maanau Lat.Dasanan Kund Kali Chhabi Lajjit Sajjit Kanak Samaan Peet Pat. [2]Muni Man Dhyaan Dharat Nahin Paavat Karat Vinod Sang Baalak Bhat.Daas Ananya Bhajan Ras Kaaran Hit Harivansh Prakat Leela Nat. [3]- Shri Hita Harivansh Mahaprabhu, Shri Hit Chaurasi (64)O Sakhī!  Śrī Kṛṣṇa plays the sweet melody of the flute at Vaṁśīvaṭa. Along the supremely sacred and beautiful banks of the Yamunā in Śrī Dhām Vṛndāvana, spring ever prevails. [1]Śrī Kṛṣṇa is adorned with a jewel-studded crown and crocodile-shaped earrings. His face is like a blooming lotus, with locks of hair swaying like bumblebees. The beauty of His teeth puts even jasmine buds to shame, and His yellow garments shine like radiant gold. [2]He who even great sages cannot attain through meditation, is delightfully sporting with His friends here. Śrī Hit Harivaṁśa Mahāprabhu says that this supremely graceful acrobat has manifested these pastimes solely to bestow the perfection of devotional rasa upon His exclusive servants. [3]

title: Mansa Baacha Karmana - Shri Biharin Dev Ji Ki Vani, Siddhant Ki Saakhi (121)
sanskrit_text: Manasa Baacha Karmana, Sarva Aatama Jaani.Shri Biharinidasi Basikaran, Fabi Priya Sukh Daani.- Shri Biharin Dev Ji, Shri Biharin Dev Ji Ki Vani, Siddhant Ki Saakhi (121)Through mind, words, deeds, and with one’s entire sense of self, one should offer oneself solely unto Śrī Nitya-Vihāriṇī Jū (Śrī Rādhā). Empowered by this very rasa, attaining the state of a maidservant of Śrī Vihāriṇī Jū and entering Her captivating sway, that Śrī Vihāriṇī-Dāsī manifests in Śrī Nikuñja-Mahāl as a source of happiness to Śrī Priyā Herself.

title: Dvai Lar Motin Ki Ek Punja  - Shri Swami Haridas Ji, Kelimal (20)
sanskrit_text: (Raag Kanharau)Dvai Lar Motin Ki Ek Punja Poti Kau SaadaNetrani Drishti Laagai Jini Meri.Haathani Chaari Chaari Churi Paaeni Ikasaar ChuraChaupahalu Ikatak Rahe Hari Heri.Ek Maragaji Saari Tan Tein Kanchuki NyariAru Anchara Ki Baaeen Gati Mori Urasani Pheri.Shriharidas Ke Swami Syama KunjbihariYa Ras Hi Bas Bhaye Harain Harain Sarakani Neri.- Shri Swami Haridas Ji, Kelimal (20)Śrī Kuñjabihāriṇī Jū (Śrī Rādhā) wears around her neck a simple necklace of two strands of pearls. O sakhī! My gaze cannot move away from her, even for a moment. [1]On each of her hands shine four bangles, and on her feet gleams a single four-sided anklet. Śrī Hari beholds her steadily, without even blinking his eyes. [2]She wears a single, maragajī (rumpled) sārī, the bodice showing distinctly, as she has twisted and drawn the left edge of the sārī over her breasts. [3]Svāminī Śyāmā Jū, the worshipful deity of Svāmī Śrī Haridās, has completely enslaved Kuñjabihārī (Śrī Kṛṣṇa) through Her love. Enchanted by Her charm, Kuñjabihārī slowly and irresistibly moves closer toward her. [4]

title: Paavan Vrinda Vipin Ki, Mahima Kahi Na Jaay - Shri Santsharan Ji
sanskrit_text: (Kundaliyan)Paavan Vrinda Vipin Ki, Mahima Kahi Na Jaay.Jaaki Raj Paavan Parasi, Paapi Jan Tari Jaay. [1]Paapi Jan Tari Jaay, Naikahu Kasht Na Paave.Radheshyaam Sunaam Rati, Dhaam Shrohaar Ko Paavai. [2]‘Sant’ Sakal Sansaar Mein, Vrindavan Man Bhaavan.Saadhu Sang Satsang So, Bane Apaavan Paavan. [3]- Shri Santsharan JiThe unfathomable glory of the supremely sacred Śrī Dhām Vṛndāvan is impossible to describe. By merely touching its holy dust, even the greatest sinner is effortlessly lifted across the ocean of material existence. [1]Such a sinner attains deliverance without any special effort or hardship. While continually chanting the sacred names of Rādhā–Śyām, he ultimately reaches the eternal abode of Śrī Hari. [2]Śrī Saṃtaśaraṇa says—in the entire world, for the community of saints, Vṛndāvan alone is the most beloved abode, because by the influence of sādhu-saṅga and satsanga there, even the most fallen of souls is effortlessly purified.  [3]

title: Yadi Kuntal Kaale Sanvaare Hi The - Braj Ke Sawaiya
sanskrit_text: (Sawaiya)Yadi Kuntal Kaale Sanvaare Hi The, To Kapolon Pai Yon Latkaana Na Tha.Jab Kajjal Rekh Lagaayi Thi To, Tirchhe Drig Baan Chalaana Na Tha. [1]Pahna Pat Peet Manohar To, Har Baar Use Fahraana Na Tha.Yah Sundar Vesh Banaaya Tha To, Is Bhaanti Hamen Tadpaana Na Tha. [2]- Braj Ke SawaiyaO Śrī Kṛṣṇa, if Your hair was already perfectly adorned, then why allow those curls to dance upon Your cheeks and enchant us so deeply? When You lined Your eyes with kohl, why did You send forth the arrows of those sidelong glances that wound our hearts with love? [1]If You wore the captivating yellow garment, then why keep fluttering it again and again, stealing every trace of our awareness? Having adorned Yourself in such beauty, why leave us to burn in the agony of separation? [2]

title: Shyam Sada Vash Priti Ke Tin Bhuvan Vikhyat - Shri Brajavasidas, Braj Vilas
sanskrit_text: Shyaam Sada Vash Preeti Ke, Teen Bhuvan Vikhyaat.Vina Preeti Nahin Paiye, Nandmahar Ko Taat.- Shri Brajavasidas, Braj VilasŚyāmasundar is always under the control of love—this truth is well known throughout the three worlds. Without pure love, Nanda Mahārāja’s son, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, can never be attained.

title: Dou Rajat Syama Syam - Sri Surdas, Soor Sagar (1696)
sanskrit_text: (Rag Devgandhar)Dou Rajat Syama Syam.Braj-Juvati-Mandali Birajati, Dekhatin Surgan-Baam. [1]Dhanya Dhanya Vrindavan Kau Sukh, Surpur Kaunain Kaam.Dhani Brishbhanu-Suta, Dhani Mohan, Dhani Gopani Kau Naam. [2]Inki Ko Dasi Sari Hwai Hai, Dhanya Sarad Ki Jaam.Kaisenhun ‘Sur’ Janam Braj Pavain, Yah Sukh Nahin Tihun Dhaam. [3]- Sri Surdas, Soor Sagar (1696)Śrī Rādhikā and Śyāmasundar are both magnificently adorned, and along with them, the entire group of the women of Vraja shines in beauty. From the sky, celestial maidens too gaze eagerly, longing for their darśan. [1]They say to one another—“This Vṛndāvan is supremely blessed, for here bliss spreads in every direction. Compared to it, even the beauty of heaven appears insignificant. Blessed is Vṛṣabhānu-nandinī Śrī Rādhā Mahārānī, blessed is Nanda-nandan Śrī Kṛṣṇa, and blessed indeed are all these gopīs.” [2]Who could ever attain a fortune equal to that of these maidservants of the divine couple, Śrī Rādhā Mādhava? Blessed is this full moon night of Śarada. How might we take birth in this Vraja to experience such bliss? In the words of Śrī Sūrdās, such nectar does not exist anywhere in the three worlds. [3]

title: Shri Vrindavan Vaas Ki Aasa Yahi Manmaani - Shri Lalit Madhuri
sanskrit_text: Shri Vrindavan Vaas Ki Aasa Yahi Manmaani. Lalit Madhuri Laal Daras Taji Aan Na Chit Aani. [1]Shri Radha Govind Kripa Aval Dridh Jiya Mein Thaani.Yugal Bihaari Lakhaun Drigan Chhavi Roop Suraskhani. [2]- Shri Lalit MadhuriI now have only one firm longing—to reside in Śrī Vṛndāvan alone. The heart of ‘Lalitamādhurī’ no longer finds even the slightest delight anywhere else, having once tasted the darśan of Śrī Lālajī. [1]Through the boundless compassion of Śrī Rādhā-Govinda, an unshakable faith in Their grace has arisen in the heart. With these very eyes, I may forever behold the enchanting form of Yugala-bihārī. [2]

title: Jugal Lagan Mein Man Magan Raakhu Aathon Yaam - Shri Saras Madhuri
sanskrit_text: Jugal Lagan Mein Man Magan Raakhu Aathon Yaam. ‘Saras Madhuri’ Surati Son, Sumirahu Shyama Shyam.- Shri Saras MadhuriKeep your mind absorbed in loving devotion of the Divine Couple, Śrī Śyāmā Śyām, throughout all eight quarters of the day. Śrī Sarasamādhurī says — with rasa-filled remembrance, meditate upon them continuously.

title: Jay Jay Shri Lalita Lalit Yugal Anandini - Shri Vanshi Ali, Shri Lalita Mangal (5)
sanskrit_text: Jai Jai Shri Lalita Lalit Jugal Anandini.Jeevan Praan Saman Su Kirati Nandini. [1]Dampati Kari Gati Rati Mati Jug Dhan Swamini.Nij Sampati Nit Vilasati Gun-Abhiramini. [2]Abhiram Gun Barnat Thake Mati Kavi Katha Kaise Lahen.Jake Prasad Prabhav Lakhi, Jiy Lal Hu Muke Rahen. [3]Seva Vivid Vidhi Chaturi, Gun Kah Sakati Nahin Radhika.Dasi Janani Nit Poshini, Priya Sahachari Sukh Sadhika. [4]- Shri Vanshi Ali, Shri Lalita Mangal (5)Glory to Śrī Lalitā Jī, who constantly intensifies the nectar of the divine couple, Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa’s mutual love. Her very life is none other than Śrī Rādhā, the beloved daughter of Śrī Kirti. [1]Her goal, mind, and love are fully dedicated to the divine couple, Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa. Thus, Śrī Lalitā Jī is called the Swāminī of the treasure, the Yugala-rasa. For her, Śrī Yugal alone is her exclusive possession, and she remains ever immersed in the rasa of the divine couple, endowed with limitless virtues. [2]Describing Śrī Lalitā Jī’s greatness and qualities tires even the intellect of the great Rasikas; capturing her true essence in words is impossible. Śrī Kṛṣṇa Himself falls silent in awe at witnessing her service, prasāda, and influence. [3]Her expertise in serving the divine couple through various kinds of services is unparalleled, and words cannot do it justice. Even Śrī Rādhā Jū cannot fully describe her glories. Śrī Lalitā Jī alone possesses such a rare qualification that she serves Śrī Rādhā eternally both in the mood of a maidservant and in the affectionate mood of a mother. Śrī Lalitā Jī is the favorite Sahchari of Śrī Rādhā, bringing immense happiness to Her. [4]

title: Man Lagyo Sukh Bhog Mein Taran Chahe Sansar - Shri Narayan Swami, Anurag Ras (51)
sanskrit_text: Mana Laagyo Sukh Bhog Mein, Taran Chahai Sansar.‘Narayan’ Kaise Bane, Divas Rain Ko Pyar.- Shri Narayan Swami, Anurag Ras (51)Śrī Nārāyaṇ Swāmī says, "When the mind remains absorbed in pleasures and sensual desires, attached to them night and day, how can one ever hope to cross the vast ocean of worldly existence?"
